value.title: Handler timing is occupancy, not CPU

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Complements the existing fixed-table telemetry and bounded-worker-lifetime notes.

#282 measures completed-handler wall time minus explicitly marked parking, NOT CPU. SQLite/I/O, lock contention and scheduler delay remain active; detached work and streamed response bodies are outside the interval. Rank route deltas to select candidates, then correlate CPU/stack/workload evidence before naming a culprit. F231 diagnosis was still open at verdict time.

HeldSpan adds to the task-local scope present at DROP, not a captured parent accumulator. Request-future migration is safe; spawned tasks do not inherit the scope. Moving a guard across tasks can lose or misattribute time; overlapping guards can double-count before the final held<=wall clamp masks it. The five shipped sites were lexical/sequential: inbox select, dispatch sleep, spawn footer/poll sleeps, revive pane-close sleep. Keep I/O outside these spans.

Cost scales with completed responses R, future polls/drops P and marked waits W. The ~40 ns release replay covered a ready, successful, held=0 path with one scope poll; it excluded HeldSpan/held-atomic costs and used a retained pre-rebase binary, not the final head. Preserve that provenance. Independent exact-source mutations caught both dropped active add and held counted as active, followed by a restored green baseline; verdict d02e559 records receipts.
